newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end up ahead of key monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end up ahead of key monetary policy.

text.p: Indian stocks scored small gains across major bourses on Friday ahead of the credit policy announcement due on Saturday, traders said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 18.19 points higher or 0.58 percent at 3,130.21, off the day's peak of 3,130.90.
The announcement of a 3 percent rise in the six-month 1996/97 (April-March) net profit of market major Reliance beat market forecasts of a fall in the firm's profits.
Shares of Reliance rose 2.0 rupees to 196.75 on volumes of over 4.9 million shares at the BSE.
The country's biggest private sector firm reported a net profit of 6.51 billion rupees against its year-ago figure of 6.33 billion.
Analysts were expecting higher costs, lower product prices and flat volume growth to cut its profits by 20-25 percent.
"Everybody is actually baffled," said Jal Irani, analyst at Jardine Fleming Broking India. "I am surprised," said analyst Prakash Joshi at W I Carr (Far East) in Bombay.
But, they said the firm's decision not to provide for a 12.9 percent minimum tax imposed in India's July federal budget on non-tax paying companies partly explained its good results.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index was up 2.93 points or 0.33 percent at 895.0.
Market participants are also awaiting the Reserve Bank of India's 1996/97 (April-March) six month credit policy due on Saturday to lend some cheer to the stock markets.
Bankers expect a cut in cash reserve requirements of banks which is expected to boost liquidity and spark a fall in interest rates.
The Delhi index ended 0.59 points down at 709.34. The Calcutta index was up 3.79 points to 420.42 and the Madras index 20.0 points to 3,215.78.
